jobs.title: VP of Data Center Development / Chief Development Officer
jobs.description:
Posh is developing data center projects and hiring a senior leader to help turn sites and plans into operating facilities. You will work directly with the founding team, bringing the development judgment and execution experience to move projects from diligence through construction, energization, and commissioning.

We expect to hire at the VP level and are open to a Chief Development Officer title for someone whose experience and scope fit. This is a hands-on leadership role with responsibility for both project strategy and day-to-day execution.

What You Will Own

Lead the development process: site feasibility, land and site control, utility coordination, entitlements, permitting, design, procurement, construction, commissioning, and operational handover.
Establish credible power, cost, and schedule assumptions. Identify critical-path constraints early, resolve dependencies, and keep the team focused on decisions that move projects forward.
Build and manage relationships with utilities, landowners, local authorities, engineering firms, general contractors, equipment vendors, and other delivery partners.
Own integrated project schedules, development budgets, risk registers, and clear go/no-go recommendations. Support project economics, commercial negotiations, and financing diligence alongside the team.
Coordinate electrical, mechanical, cooling, network, and operational requirements with technical experts so customer needs translate into a buildable, commissionable facility.
Build the development team and external partner network as projects grow, while staying close enough to the details to unblock work personally.

USE AI TO BUILD FASTER

We want someone curious about new tools and willing to change how development gets done. Partner with our team to use AI for tasks such as site screening, diligence synthesis, permit tracking, bid comparison, schedule analysis, and project reporting. Test useful workflows, measure their impact, and verify outputs against source documents and expert judgment. You do not need to be a software engineer; you do need the willingness to learn and put better tools into practice.

What You Bring

Direct responsibility for delivering at least one data center through construction and commissioning or operational handover. You can clearly explain your role, the facility's scale, major constraints, and the outcome.
Experience leading complex development or capital projects, managing budgets and schedules, and coordinating multidisciplinary teams and external partners.
Practical understanding of utility service and energization, permitting, long-lead equipment, contractor delivery, and commissioning dependencies.
Commercial judgment: you can weigh speed, cost, reliability, and execution risk and make clear recommendations with incomplete information.
A hands-on approach, strong follow-through, and comfort working in a small team where leaders both set direction and execute.
Demonstrated curiosity about AI and automation, with a concrete example of a workflow you have improved or a thoughtful proposal you are ready to test.

Experience with high-density AI infrastructure, power-constrained sites, onsite energy systems, or developing multiple facilities is a plus. We value what you have delivered and how you work more than a particular prior title.

TO APPLY

Send your background and a brief description of one or two data center projects you helped deliver. Include approximate MW, your personal responsibilities, the stage you joined, the stage you delivered, and a difficult problem you solved. Share one example of how you have used—or would use—AI to accelerate development. Please omit confidential information from prior employers or clients.

jobs.description:
Overview

Utah State University Extension is seeking an experienced, collaborative, and forward-thinking leader to serve as Executive Director & Extension Professor – Agriculture, Natural Resources & Strategic Centers. Based at Utah State University’s main campus in Logan, Utah, this position provides statewide leadership for Extension’s agriculture, natural resources, and strategic center portfolio and also serves as the State Agriculture Extension Program Leader.

As a Senior Leader Within USU Extension, The Executive Director Provides Strategic Leadership And Administrative Oversight For a Diverse Portfolio Of Extension Programs, Centers, Facilities, And Statewide Initiatives, Including

Extension Agriculture & Natural Resources Department
Davis Agricultural Heritage Center
USU Botanical Center
Ogden Botanical Gardens
Swaner Preserve & EcoCenter

Reporting to the Vice President of USU Extension, the Executive Director works across these areas to establish strategic direction, align people and resources, strengthen partnerships, support organizational leaders, and increase the collective impact of Extension programs and facilities throughout Utah.

This position serves as a leader of leaders, providing direction, support, and accountability to directors, faculty, and personnel responsible for the day-to-day leadership of programs and centers within the portfolio.

The Executive Director also serves as a member of USU Extension's senior leadership team, contributing to organization-wide strategy, resource planning, policy development, and decision-making.

While each area within the portfolio has a distinct mission, audience, and expertise, the Executive Director is responsible for identifying opportunities to connect programs, people, facilities, partnerships, and resources in ways that strengthen USU Extension's statewide mission and service to Utah communities. The successful candidate would be expected to represent USU Extension at social and donor events, industry conferences, and other events where USU Extension leadership is expected to represent USU with distinction. This position requires frequent statewide travel as well as frequent evening and weekend work.

Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership

Provide executive leadership and strategic direction for Agriculture & Natural Resources and the centers and initiatives within the assigned portfolio.
Establish priorities that align with USU Extension and Utah State University goals.
Translate organizational priorities into actionable plans and measurable outcomes.
Work with faculty and staff to establish goals, priorities, and expectations for their respective areas.
Identify emerging opportunities, challenges, and needs throughout Utah and position Extension to respond effectively.
Advise Extension executive leadership regarding programs, facilities, personnel, resources, partnerships, risks, and opportunities.
Lead and support organizational change and strategic initiatives.
Identify opportunities for collaboration across programs and centers while preserving the distinct mission and strengths of each area.

Agriculture & Natural Resources

Provide executive leadership for USU Extension's statewide agriculture and natural resources portfolio.
Support Extension faculty, staff, specialists, programs, and initiatives serving Utah's agricultural producers, landowners, communities, industries, home horticulture, and natural resources.
Strengthen connections among county and statewide Extension programming, academic departments, researchers, industry, government agencies, and community partners.
Support development of responsive programming addressing current and emerging agricultural and natural resource needs.
Encourage interdisciplinary approaches that connect university expertise with practical needs throughout Utah.
Identify opportunities to strengthen, expand, and sustain high-impact Extension programming.
Advocate for the personnel, financial, and program resources necessary to support effective statewide delivery.

Strategic Centers & Facilities

Provide executive leadership and long-term strategic direction for the USU Botanical Center, Davis Agricultural Heritage Center, Ogden Botanical Gardens and Swaner Preserve & EcoCenter.
Support the distinct educational, agricultural, horticultural, environmental, conservation, research, demonstration, and community-facing missions of the centers.
Work with center leadership to establish long-term strategic and operational priorities.
Provide strategic oversight for significant Extension facilities, land, equipment, and other physical assets.
Identify opportunities to increase utilization, programming, partnerships, visibility, and community impact.
Coordinate facility, capital, maintenance, and infrastructure priorities with appropriate university partners.
Support sustainable operational and financial models for Extension centers.
Encourage collaboration among centers and other Extension programs when shared expertise, facilities, or resources can increase impact.
Ensure responsible stewardship of university facilities, land, equipment, and other resources.

Organizational Leadership & People Development

Provide direct leadership, supervision, coaching, and development to county Agriculture and Natural Resources faculty and program coordinators. There are approximately 50 direct reports.
Administrate the promotion and tenure process for county faculty in the Agriculture and Natural Resources department.
Build a strong and collaborative leadership team across programs and centers.
Establish clear roles, responsibilities, decision-making authority, expectations, and accountability.
Support faculty in addressing complex organizational, personnel, programmatic, and operational issues.
Evaluate organizational structures and workforce needs and recommend changes when appropriate.
Oversee and support recruitment, retention, professional development, and succession planning.
Foster a culture of collaboration, professionalism, innovation, transparency, accountability, service, and responsible stewardship.
Encourage communication and collaboration across geographically dispersed personnel and programs.

Financial & Resource Stewardship

Provide strategic oversight of financial, personnel, facility, and program resources across the portfolio.
Work collaboratively with Extension executive leadership and Extension Business Services to establish funding and resource priorities.
Provide strategic direction regarding allocation and use of resources while maintaining appropriate financial controls and administrative responsibilities.
Review financial and operational performance and identify areas requiring attention or investment.
Evaluate the long-term financial sustainability of programs, centers, facilities, and initiatives.
Support development of grants, gifts, partnerships, program revenues, and other external resources.
Ensure resources are aligned with Extension priorities and used responsibly.
Promote accountability and stewardship of state, federal, county, grant, gift, program-generated, and other university resources.

Partnerships & External Relations

Develop and maintain strong relationships with county and municipal governments, state and federal agencies, agricultural organizations, industry, businesses, nonprofit organizations, community partners, donors, and other stakeholders.
Represent USU Extension in appropriate statewide, regional, university, and community discussions.
Identify opportunities for collaborative programming, shared investment, and strategic partnerships.
Strengthen connections between university expertise and the needs of Utah communities.
Work with Extension and university leadership to develop partnerships that advance organizational priorities.
Serve as an advocate for the programs, people, centers, and communities represented within the portfolio.

Innovation, Program Development & Impact

Encourage innovation and responsible experimentation across Extension programs and centers.
Support development and implementation of new programs responsive to emerging needs.
Establish expectations for evaluation, outcomes, and organizational performance.
Use data, program outcomes, financial information, and stakeholder feedback to inform decisions.
Communicate accomplishments, outcomes, opportunities, and challenges to Extension executive leadership.

Policy, Compliance & Risk Management

Commitment:

Compensation:
Commission and equity; no guaranteed salary at the outset
SportsWrap Productions is seeking an experienced, entrepreneurial partnership executive to become our Founding Director of Partnerships.
This is an opportunity to build the commercial partnership operation for a rapidly growing independent sports-media company with national television distribution and an expanding digital, podcast, newsletter and social-media presence.
SportsWrap Productions is the company behind SportsWrap w/Jason Page , a nationally syndicated daily sports television program available through more than 270 affiliates, regional sports networks and Game+ in Canada. SportsWrap is available in more than 110 million U.S. television homes and receives more than 5,000 television airings each month.
Our digital ecosystem includes YouTube, TikTok, Instagram, Facebook, X, the SportsWrap podcast and The Daily Wrap newsletter.
The Opportunity The Founding Director of Partnerships will work directly with founder and host Jason Page to identify, develop and close revenue-generating relationships with brands, advertisers and strategic partners.
This is not a traditional salaried position at the outset. Compensation will consist of commission on partnership revenue generated by the Director, along with an equity opportunity reflecting the individual’s role in helping build the company’s commercial operation.
The ideal candidate will see this as an opportunity to create meaningful recurring revenue, participate in the growth of the company and potentially develop the position into a full-time salaried leadership role as revenue supports it.
Primary Responsibilities Build and manage a pipeline of prospective national and regional partners.
Identify brands that align with SportsWrap’s audience, programming and multiplatform distribution.
Develop and pitch integrated partnership concepts across television, digital video, social media, podcasts and newsletters.
Sell traditional commercial inventory as well as branded segments, presenting sponsorships, content integrations and larger strategic partnerships.
Lead outreach, presentations, negotiations and closing activity.
Work with SportsWrap’s leadership to establish pricing, packaging and category strategy.
Maintain organized records of prospects, conversations, proposals and projected revenue.
Help develop a repeatable sponsorship-sales process that can grow with the company.
Represent SportsWrap professionally with agencies, brands and other potential partners.

Who We’re Looking For The strongest candidate will have:
Demonstrated experience in media sales, sponsorships, brand partnerships, advertising or business development.
Existing relationships with brands, agencies or marketing decision-makers.
A history of developing opportunities and closing business—not simply generating introductions.
An understanding of multiplatform sports media and integrated sponsorships.
The ability to create customized ideas rather than relying exclusively on standard advertising packages.
Strong written, presentation, negotiation and relationship-management skills.
The independence and discipline to succeed in a remote, results-driven role.
An entrepreneurial mindset and comfort joining a growing company before a traditional salary structure is available.

Experience in sports media, television, digital media, podcasts, branded content, sports betting, automotive, consumer products, travel, hospitality, food and beverage, financial services or technology is especially valuable.
Compensation and Growth This position begins as a commission-and-equity opportunity without a guaranteed salary.
The selected candidate will receive:
Commission on partnership revenue personally sourced and closed, payable under a written commission agreement.
The opportunity to earn meaningful equity in SportsWrap Productions, subject to an agreed vesting schedule and performance expectations.
Direct access to the company’s founder and involvement in major commercial decisions.
The opportunity to build and eventually lead SportsWrap’s broader partnerships and revenue operation.
The potential to transition into a salaried executive position when company revenue supports that move.

The initial expectation is a minimum of 10–15 hours per week, with flexibility based on opportunity and deal activity. The first-year objective is to generate approximately $100,000–$250,000 in new partnership revenue.
This role is best suited for someone who believes in the potential of independent sports media, wants their performance to create genuine ownership value and is motivated by building something—not simply maintaining an existing sales book.
About SportsWrap SportsWrap delivers the conversations sports fans actually want to have—without league agendas, network politics or corporate talking points.
Since launching in January 2024, SportsWrap w/Jason Page has grown from approximately 50 television affiliates to more than 270, with distribution across the United States and Canada. The company is now building the partnership and revenue infrastructure needed to support its next phase of growth.
How to Apply Please send a résumé or LinkedIn profile along with a short introduction explaining:
Your relevant sales and partnership experience.
The types of brands or agencies with which you have relationships.
An example of a partnership you helped develop or close.
Why a commission-and-equity opportunity with SportsWrap interests you.

Candidates should apply only if they understand and are comfortable with the position beginning without guaranteed salary compensation.
